cards.explanation: The answer is Zedekiah king of Judah. The LORD tells Jeremiah the prophet to go and speak to him (Jeremiah 34:2). Jeremiah's message goes straight to the man wearing the crown. I'd be sweating just walking up to him with this news, friends, and I only deliver cookies.

The answer is that he'll burn it down. The LORD says, “Behold, I am about to deliver this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.” (Jeremiah 34:2) It's a hard line to open with. The LORD says plainly what is coming, and that's why the rest of the chapter matters.

The answer is True. The LORD tells Zedekiah, “And you yourself will not escape his grasp, but will surely be captured and delivered into his hand.” (Jeremiah 34:3) The king can't slip out a back door. The word is surely, and that's a firm word.

The answer is Babylon. The LORD says to Zedekiah, “…you will go to Babylon.” (Jeremiah 34:3) He's captured, he meets the king of Babylon, and then he goes to the king's own country. That's a long trip, friends.

The answer is peace. The LORD says, “You will not die by the sword; you will die in peace.” (Jeremiah 34:4-5) That comes right after the hard news about capture and Babylon. It's a gentle line in a rough message, and it ends with the LORD saying He Himself has spoken it.

The answer is that people will burn spices and lament for him. The LORD says, “As spices were burned for your fathers, the former kings who preceded you, so people will burn spices for you and lament…” (Jeremiah 34:5) Zedekiah gets the same honor the earlier kings got. Burning spices is the kind of thing that fills a whole room, and the people grieve out loud.

The answer is False. The text says Babylon's army is fighting against Lachish and Azekah, and “…these were the only fortified cities remaining in Judah.” (Jeremiah 34:7) Only two strongholds are left standing. That's about as close to empty as a cookie jar at midnight.

The answer is True. The word from the LORD is “…that each man should free his Hebrew slaves, both male and female, and no one should hold his fellow Jew in bondage.” (Jeremiah 34:9) Men and women both. Nobody gets left off the list.

The answer is that their freedom lasts until the people change their minds. The people agreed and released them, “…but later they changed their minds and took back the menservants and maidservants they had freed…” (Jeremiah 34:10-11) The text says they forced them to become slaves again. I think that one hurts, friends, because the freedom ended only because the people changed their minds.

The answer is seventh. The LORD says, “Every seventh year, each of you must free his Hebrew brother who has sold himself to you. He may serve you six years, but then you must let him go free.” (Jeremiah 34:14) Six years of service, then he goes free. The LORD said it plainly when He brought them out of Egypt.

The answer is False. After giving the law about freeing a Hebrew brother in the seventh year, the LORD says, “But your fathers did not listen or incline their ear.” (Jeremiah 34:14) They didn't follow it. That makes the people's recent freedom proclamation stand out.

The answer is in the house of the LORD. The LORD says they made the covenant “…before Me in the house that bears My Name.” (Jeremiah 34:15) That's His house, with His Name on it. They made the promise right there, in front of Him.

The answer is free to go wherever they wanted. The LORD says the servants were “…set at liberty to go wherever they wanted…” (Jeremiah 34:16) That's real freedom, with no strings. Then the people took them back and forced them to be slaves again, and that makes the turnaround hit harder.

The answer is freedom to fall by sword and plague and famine. The LORD says, “So now I proclaim freedom for you, declares the LORD…” and then names it: “…freedom to fall by sword, by plague, and by famine!” (Jeremiah 34:17) The people wouldn't proclaim freedom for their brothers, so the LORD uses their own word back at them. This one is heavy, friends, and I think it's okay to let it sit.

The answer is by passing between the pieces of a calf. The LORD speaks of “…the calf they cut in two in order to pass between its pieces.” (Jeremiah 34:18) It's how they sealed the covenant before Him. And the LORD says those who broke the covenant He will treat like that calf.

The answer is False. The LORD lists “The officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the pieces of the calf…” (Jeremiah 34:19) The priests are on the list, but so are the officials and all the people of the land. It was a crowd, not just one group.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “I will deliver into the hands of their enemies who seek their lives.” (Jeremiah 34:20) It covers the officials, the priests and all the people who passed between the pieces of the calf. This is a heavy part, friends, and the LORD doesn't soften it.

The answer is that He'll bring them back to this city. The LORD says, “Behold, I am going to give the command, declares the LORD, and I will bring them back to this city.” (Jeremiah 34:22) The army that had withdrawn comes back, and the LORD says it will fight against the city. He is the One giving the command.

The answer is desolation. The LORD says, “And I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.” (Jeremiah 34:22) It's the last line of the chapter, and it's a heavy way to close. The cities stand empty.
